Short answer

To install herdr on Omarchy, open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add herdr. It is a 7.8 MB download (21.7 MB installed), version 0.9.1-2, licensed Apache-2.0. Herdr terminal workspace manager for AI coding agents. Free and open source.

Install herdr on Omarchy

Herdr is a Rust-based terminal session manager purpose-built for running multiple AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and similar tools) at once. It works like tmux or screen, keeping sessions alive through disconnects or reboots and letting you reattach from anywhere, but it also detects each agent's state, working, blocked, done, or idle, and shows it in a sidebar so you're not hunting for a stuck agent. It runs inside your existing terminal (ghostty, alacritty, kitty, wezterm) with no Electron overhead.

Watch: Herdr in about 6 minutes ↗

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add herdr
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 0.9.1-2:
    pacman -Qi herdr

Open and use herdr

herdr has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql herdr | grep /usr/bin/

Frequently asked questions

How do I install herdr on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add herdr. The download is 7.8 MB and it takes 21.7 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is herdr free?

Free and open source. The package is licensed Apache-2.0.

How do I uninstall herdr?

Run omarchy pkg drop herdr. It removes the package from your system.

What does herdr depend on?

The package declares 2 dependencies: gcc-libs, glibc. Omarchy installs them for you.

Is herdr a desktop app?

No. herdr has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is herdr in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as herdr (version 0.9.1-2) in the official Omarchy package repository. Herdr makes it. Project site: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr.
